items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to be enough to get most of the benefit, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try to avoid eating dinner late, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners in the program. Only 8.3% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later, so you're already on the right track.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You're doing well with your overnight fast, averaging 12.0 hours and sometimes reaching 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed some numbers, but the program didn't find a clear link in real people yet.
